About the Role
How do you translate evolving financial crime regulations into practical, effective KYC processes?

We are looking for experienced KYC Process Specialists to support an AMLR implementation project within the banking sector. Working closely with internal process experts and project drivers, you will help translate new and updated AML/CTF regulatory requirements into detailed process changes and operational guidance.

You will play an important role in ensuring that updated KYC requirements are effectively implemented across the entire process lifecycle. The initiatives cover areas such as PEP requirements, Purpose and Nature of Relationship, customer risk scoring, adverse media screening and ongoing due diligence.

Key Responsibilities
• 
Work closely with internal process experts and project drivers to operationalise AMLR-related requirements.

• 
Translate external AMLR and Regulatory Technical Standards (RTS), together with updated internal AML/CTF rules, into detailed process changes.

• 
Define and document changes to KYC processes to ensure effective end-to-end implementation of the new requirements.

• 
Support the implementation of updated requirements related to Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs).

• 
Define process updates concerning Purpose and Nature of Relationship requirements.

• 
Develop procedural updates related to customer risk scoring changes.

• 
Support changes to adverse media screening processes.

• 
Implement operational changes related to Ongoing Due Diligence (ODD) cycle requirements.

• 
Develop clear instructions and guidance for operational staff.

• 
Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to ensure consistent operationalisation of regulatory requirements.

Qualifications and ExperienceMust-Have Requirements
• 
Strong knowledge of Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Counter-Terrorist Financing (CTF).

• 
Good understanding of Know Your Customer (KYC) processes.

• 
Experience working with KYC, Financial Crime or business process development and change initiatives.

• 
Strong analytical skills and the ability to assess complex requirements.

• 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

• 
CV must be submitted in English.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications
• 
Legal background or relevant legal knowledge.

• 
Ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical operational processes.

• 
Ability to explain complex regulatory matters clearly and simply.

• 
Knowledge of Ongoing Due Diligence (ODD) requirements.

• 
Familiarity with PEP requirements, Purpose and Nature of Relationship, adverse media screening and customer risk scoring.

jobs.occupation: Researcher in Mooring Design and Analysis for Offshore Floating Solar Farms
jobs.description:
About the position
A fixed-term 100% researcher position is available at the University of Agder, Faculty of Engineering and Science as a Researcher in Structural Engineering, affiliated to the Department of Engineering Sciences, for a period of 2 years. The position is located at Campus Grimstad.  The starting date is Spring 2027. 

The Department of Engineering Sciences has more than 90 employees in scientific positions, and more than 1500 students at all levels. A variety of research is conducted within all the groups; Mechatronics, Renewable Energy, Civil Engineering and Industrial Economy, and we also welcome interdisciplinary projects within the department or with other research groups. This position will be associated with the Civil Engineering section. We have a broad international cooperation, and close collaboration with industrial partners and public services in the region. This is a benefit both for teaching and research. The partners contribute with assignments, competence and resources.Project Background

As one of the projects successfully funded by the CETPartnership, HelioSea aims to develop and demonstrate an innovative floating photovoltaic (FPV) concept for marine environments. The technology integrates a tension-leg platform, dual-axis solar tracking, and intelligent operational control. Through the design, deployment, and monitored operation of a pilot system, the project aims to advance the concept from Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 3 to TRL 5.
Responsibilities
The researcher will contribute to the work package focused on advancing offshore solar farms. The work package involves five project partners and includes the following tasks:

• Numerical modelling of shared mooring configurations;
• Wave-basin testing of FPV farms;
• Analysis of FPV farms co-located with floating breakwaters; and
• Assessment of farm-level energy production and power performance.
The focus of this position will be the design of shared mooring and cable layouts. The researcher may also support experimental testing and pilot activities. The work will include dynamic response analyses, covering both hydrodynamic and aerodynamic effects, as well as structural integrity analyses.

The researcher will collaborate closely with project partners, including partners from Spain and Portugal, to carry out the project activities. The research will involve preparing and submitting project reports and high-quality scientific publications, as well as contributing to dissemination activities at the European level.
Required qualifications
• A PhD in marine technology, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, or another relevant field. Applicants must have had their doctoral thesis approved by the application deadline.
• Expertise in at least one of the following areas: Fluid dynamics; Design of marine structures; Offshore multibody structures; Multiphysics simulation of marine and offshore structures; Experimental analysis of marine structure.Desired qualifications
• A strong record of high-quality scientific publications;
• Strong programming and analytical skills; and
• Experience working collaboratively in international research projects.
Emphasis will be placed upon the project description and the relevance it has with regard to the subject in question and the research environment at the Faculty. 

Personal qualities and suitability for the position will be emphasised.
We offer
• professional development in a large, exciting and socially influential organisation 
• a positive, inclusive and diverse working environment 
• modern facilities and a comprehensive set of welfare offers  
• membership of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
More about working at UiA.

The position is remunerated according to the State Salary Scale, salary plan 17.510, code 1109, NOK 680 000 – 730 000,- gross salary per year. Higher salary grades may be considered for particularly well-qualified applicants. A compulsory pension contribution to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund is deducted from the pay according to current statutory provisions.
General information
UiA is an open and inclusive university. We believe that diversity enriches the UiA is an open and inclusive university. We believe that diversity enriches the workplace and makes us better. We, therefore, encourage qualified candidates to apply for the position independent of gender, age, cultural background, disability or an incomplete CV. The successful applicant will have rights and obligations in accordance with the current regulations for the position, and organizational changes and changes in the duties and responsibilities of the position must be expected. The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning the acts relating to Control of Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Appointment is made by the University of Agder’s Appointments Committee for Teaching and Research Positions.  

A background check may be conducted to verify information that appears in available documents. Background checks are always done with the applicant's consent, and employment in the position requires an approved background check. Relevant applicants will receive further information. 

Short-listed applicants will be invited for interviews and a demonstration of their teaching competency, usually in the form of a trial lecture. With permission from the applicant the university also will conduct a reference check before appointment. The final recommendation will be an overall assessment based on the expert assessment, the trial lecture, the interview(s) and references. Read more about the employment process.  

In accordance with the Freedom of Information Act § 25 (2), applicants may request that they are not identified in the open list of applicants. The University, however, reserves the right to publish the names of applicants. Applicants will be advised of the University’s intention to exercise this right.
Application
The application and any necessary information about education and experience (including diplomas and certificates) are to be sent electronically. Use the link "Apply for this job".

The following documentation must be uploaded electronically: 

• Transcripts from PhD, master, and bachelor studies with grades
• CV with detailed education and work experience
• Up to 10 academic articles and R&D projects which the candidate wishes to particularly emphasise for the assessment process 
• A brief project description on the topic of mooring design for FPV array (max 2 pages)
• PhD diploma and thesis
The applicant is fully responsible for submitting complete digital documentation before the closing date. All documentation must be available in a Scandinavian language or English. 

Application deadline: 10.01.27.
Contact
For questions about the position: 

• Professor Zhiyu Jiang, tel. +47 451 01 672, e-mail: zhiyu.jiang@uia.no or 
• Head of Department Paul Ragnar Svennevig, tel. 37 23 32 54, e-mail: paul.r.svennevig@uia.no
For questions about the application process:

• HR-adviser Heidi Kristensen tel. +47 38 14 13 79, e-mail  heidi.kristensen@uia.no Creating knowledge together
When people who are committed come together to further knowledge, anything is possible.

Game communities are where players make friends, build worlds and create together. Most of the harm in them comes from a handful of users. Some are bullies who drive other players away. In a game built for kids, one of them can be an adult pretending to be twelve. Aiba builds the AI that finds them before a moderator has to, so the community stays a safe place to play and create. For studios, that means happier players, higher NPS and lower churn.

Our platform is called Amanda. It moderates chat, voice and images in real time, flags grooming, bullying and fake profiles, and gives moderators the tools to act fast. Teams at MoviestarPlanet, WildWorks and Rovio (Angry Birds) use it to keep their communities safe.

The timing is on our side. Rules like the DSA and COPPA have made online safety a requirement, not a nice-to-have. Game studios and social platforms now have to solve this, and they are coming to us to do it.

We are a small team in Oslo and Gjøvik. We need the person who turns our partners into a steady source of new customers.

The role in short
We have 3 to 5 prospective partners who could bring us customers. Today we don't work with them in a structured way. You change that. You own every partner relationship, build the method for how we work together, and make things happen.

You also measure it. You build the reporting that shows what each partner brings in. When the data shows a partner sends us the right customers, you double down.

What you'll do
• 
Own the relationship with every prospective partner, from the first conversation to a partnership that delivers.

• 
Build our partnership methodology: how we choose partners, work with them and follow up. There isn't one yet.

• 
Set up reporting on the results of the partnership motion, and share it with the team.

• 
Use the data to double down on the partners that bring in ICP opportunities.

• 
Create the content partners need to recommend and sell Amanda.

• 
Keep Aiba top of mind with every partner, so we're the first name they think of.

• 
Run partner events and joint activities that keep the relationships active.

• 
Work closely with sales and marketing, and hand warm opportunities to our Account Executives.

Who you are
• 
You have 2 to 3 years of experience in partnerships.

• 
You can turn a friendly intro into a partnership with real results.

• 
You like numbers. You'd rather show what a partner delivers than talk about it.

• 
You build relationships as easily with suits as with gamers in hoodies.

• 
You act before anyone asks. Low ego, high agency.

• 
You take feedback well, and you have a sense of humor. Both get used here.

• 
Your English is great, spoken and written. More languages are a plus.

A bonus, not a must: startup or scale-up experience, a background in gaming or edtech, or knowledge of Trust & Safety.

Who this isn't for
If you want a partner program that's already built, with a playbook and a manager who plans your week, you won't like it here.

What you get
• 
Starting at NOK 750,000+ base, plus commission paid quarterly

• 
Commission on two things: how partnerships convert into business, and partner engagement, like the partner events you run

• 
Real impact. You build the partner channel from scratch, and in a team this size, it visibly moves the company.

• 
A fast track for your commercial career, in an industry that is growing fast

• 
A product you don't have to oversell. It keeps players safe, kids included.

• 
Conferences around the world, a passionate team, and the usual Norwegian basics: pension, paid holiday and parental leave

How to apply
Apply on The Hub. It takes two minutes. First a short call with The Hub's team, then you meet the team at Aiba.

This is one of three commercial roles Aiba is hiring for right now. The other two, Account Executive and Sales Development Representative, are on The Hub too.

Om arbeidsgiveren:
At Aiba.ai, we provide an advanced AI-powered platform designed to elevate player safety by moderating in-game chat in real time. As the gaming industry expands globally, the need for a scalable solution to combat harmful behaviors is critical. Our platform safeguards communities against online threats such as bullying, grooming, racism, radicalization, and other harmful content.

Our AI technology, developed in collaboration with the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), combines machine learning algorithms and behavioral biometrics to ensure fast detection of harmful behavior. We analyze player interactions in real time, identifying threats as they occur, even when players use slang, dialects, or emojis.

Aiba.ai efficiently manages large volumes of player reports, helping developers prioritize critical issues while reducing the burden on moderation teams. This saves time and resources, ensuring swift resolution of urgent matters and improving player experience.

Our platform ensures compliance with key regulatory frameworks, including COPPA and the DSA, protecting players while keeping your game in line with evolving regulations. Our solution also leverages behavioral biometrics to track patterns of behavior, identifying repeat offenders and reducing harmful interactions over time.

Aiba.ai is scalable, supporting both indie games and large multiplayer platforms. Our APIs are customizable and easy to integrate into existing systems, allowing you to tailor moderation based on your needs. Additionally, our platform supports multiple languages, making it ideal for global games with diverse player bases. We provide real-time moderation across languages, ensuring all players are protected, regardless of location or language.

By offering advanced moderation and behavior detection, Aiba.ai helps developers create safer, more enjoyable player experiences. We reduce the burden on moderation teams, ensure regulatory compliance, and improve the health of gaming communities. Our commitment is to provide a robust, scalable solution that protects your players and helps foster a positive gaming environment.

Game communities are where players make friends, build worlds and create together. Most of the harm in them comes from a handful of users. Some are bullies who drive other players away. In a game built for kids, one of them can be an adult pretending to be twelve. Aiba builds the AI that finds them before a moderator has to, so the community stays a safe place to play and create. For studios, that means happier players, higher NPS and lower churn.

Our platform is called Amanda. It moderates chat, voice and images in real time, flags grooming, bullying and fake profiles, and gives moderators the tools to act fast. Teams at MoviestarPlanet, WildWorks and Rovio (Angry Birds) use it to keep their communities safe.

The timing is on our side. Rules like the DSA and COPPA have made online safety a requirement, not a nice-to-have. Game studios and social platforms now have to solve this, and they are coming to us to do it.

We are a small team in Oslo and Gjøvik. We need the person who turns that interest into real sales conversations.

The role in short
You own the Education stage of our pipeline. Leads come in curious but cold. You warm them up, show them why Amanda fits their community, and turn the right ones into real opportunities for our Account Executives. You work from a set list of clearly defined ICP customers, so you always know where to spend your time.

Most of our pipeline starts at events. Before a conference, you fill the calendars of our management and sales team with the right meetings. Before a community dinner, you make sure the right people have a seat at the table. Afterwards, you follow up until a good conversation becomes a customer.

What you'll do
• 
Nurture and warm up leads in the Education stage, and convert them into opportunities in the sales pipeline.

• 
Work from a set list of clearly defined ICP customers. You'll know exactly who they are and why Amanda fits them.

• 
Own our most important source of pipeline: events, conferences and community dinners around the world.

• 
Book sales meetings for management and the sales team before every event.

• 
Fill our community dinners with the right people.

• 
Follow up after every event, so meetings and dinners turn into customers over time.

• 
Work closely with our community director, and help create the marketing content that brings leads in.

• 
Pick up the phone. Some outbound cold calling is part of the job, but it isn't the whole job.

Who you are
• 
You have 1 to 2 years of experience as an SDR.

• 
You love organizing. A packed event calendar with zero double bookings is a good week for you.

• 
You write well, and you're comfortable on the phone.

• 
You build relationships as easily with suits as with gamers.

• 
You act before anyone asks. Low ego, high agency.

• 
You take feedback well, and you have a sense of humor. Both get used here.

• 
Your English is greatexcellent, spoken and written. More languages are a plus.

A bonus, not a must: startup or scale-up experience, a background in gaming or edtech, or knowledge of Trust & Safety.

Who this isn't for
If you want a pure cold-calling job, this isn't it. If you want a finished playbook and a manager who plans your week, you won't like it here either.

What you get
• 
Starting at NOK 600,000+ base, plus commission paid quarterly

• 
Commission on two things: how many of your sales-accepted leads become sales-qualified (SAL to SQL), and the ARR you and your AE pod sell each quarter

• 
Real impact. In a team this size, the pipeline you build visibly moves the company.

• 
A fast track for your commercial career, in an industry that is growing fast

• 
A product you don't have to oversell. It keeps players safe, kids included.

• 
Conferences around the world, a passionate team, and the usual Norwegian basics: pension, paid holiday and parental leave

How to apply
Apply on The Hub. It takes two minutes. First a short call with The Hub's team, then you meet the team at Aiba.

This is one of three commercial roles Aiba is hiring for right now. The other two, Account Executive and Partnership Manager, are on The Hub too.

Om arbeidsgiveren:
At Aiba.ai, we provide an advanced AI-powered platform designed to elevate player safety by moderating in-game chat in real time. As the gaming industry expands globally, the need for a scalable solution to combat harmful behaviors is critical. Our platform safeguards communities against online threats such as bullying, grooming, racism, radicalization, and other harmful content.

Our AI technology, developed in collaboration with the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), combines machine learning algorithms and behavioral biometrics to ensure fast detection of harmful behavior. We analyze player interactions in real time, identifying threats as they occur, even when players use slang, dialects, or emojis.

Aiba.ai efficiently manages large volumes of player reports, helping developers prioritize critical issues while reducing the burden on moderation teams. This saves time and resources, ensuring swift resolution of urgent matters and improving player experience.

Our platform ensures compliance with key regulatory frameworks, including COPPA and the DSA, protecting players while keeping your game in line with evolving regulations. Our solution also leverages behavioral biometrics to track patterns of behavior, identifying repeat offenders and reducing harmful interactions over time.

Aiba.ai is scalable, supporting both indie games and large multiplayer platforms. Our APIs are customizable and easy to integrate into existing systems, allowing you to tailor moderation based on your needs. Additionally, our platform supports multiple languages, making it ideal for global games with diverse player bases. We provide real-time moderation across languages, ensuring all players are protected, regardless of location or language.

By offering advanced moderation and behavior detection, Aiba.ai helps developers create safer, more enjoyable player experiences. We reduce the burden on moderation teams, ensure regulatory compliance, and improve the health of gaming communities. Our commitment is to provide a robust, scalable solution that protects your players and helps foster a positive gaming environment.

We are looking for someone with a strong passion for retail, sales and technology, who is highly driven and has a natural ability to inspire, engage and motivate others. You enjoy building long-term relationships and have a genuine interest in Samsung and its innovative product range.

As a Retail Specialist for Samsung, you will be an important brand ambassador, responsible for strengthening Samsung's position among retailers in your assigned district. An important part of your role is to ensure that retail staff have the right knowledge, confidence and tools to present and sell Samsung's Home Appliances products in the best possible way.

Who are we?

Founded on the belief that a country’s natural resources belong to its citizens, the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) brings together governments, civil society and companies to improve natural resource governance. With over 50 member countries and 60 supporting companies, the EITI promotes transparency, accountability and informed policymaking in the extractive sector. 

Behind this ambitious and impactful organisation is a diverse and dynamic team of experts working together to advance the EITI mission. Based in Oslo, Norway, the EITI International Secretariat comprises a collaborative, multinational and multilingual team of around 60 professionals who value growth and development, strong relationships, open dialogue and inclusive leadership.

What are we looking for

We are seeking an Oslo-based, experienced and highly organised person to support the Executive Director and Board Chair. The successful candidate will have strong interpersonal and organisational skills and exercise discretion and confidentiality when handling correspondence and other sensitive information.The role requires excellent time management and the ability to prioritise competing demands, manage multiple tasks and maintain close attention to detail. A proactive approach to problem-solving, a willingness to take on a variety of responsibilities and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment are essential. The role will report to the Executive Director. 

Duties and responsibilities
• Coordinate travel authorisations and confirm budget availability in line with relevant policies.
• Plan missions with country teams, including travel bookings, visa applications, itineraries and transport.
• Arrange meetings and compile materials needed for travel and missions.
• Prepare travel claims and track expenses in accordance with relevant policies.
• Monitor the Executive Director’s and Board Chair’s inboxes and urgent messages, draft approved correspondence and follow up with staff and EITI stakeholders.
• Ensure the Executive Director’s leave and working hours are accurately recorded.
• Maintain and archive the Senior Management Team’s agenda items, and coordinate meeting agendas in line with internal policies.
• Support engagement with the supporting countries constituency by scheduling meetings and liaising with the Finance Manager on reporting and budget queries.
• Schedule Senior Management Team meetings, invite relevant colleagues and record and communicate decisions and action points.
• Coordinate Senior Management Team activities, including assistance in organising retreats and the coordination of leave schedules.
• Provide targeted administrative support across the Secretariat, including assisting the Operations team when needed and helping to coordinate internal events, recognising the close links between the team’s work and support for the Executive Director and Board Chair.Qualifications
Required:

• Bachelor's degree, preferably in Business Administration or similar.
• Minimum 3 years’ experience as an executive assistant or office administrative assistant.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 tools (e.g. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and digital finance/travel systems.
• Demonstrated ability to learn new digital systems quickly.
• Working knowledge of data management and data protection (GDPR) principles.
Desirable:

• Experience working in an international environment and with international organisations.
• Working knowledge of French and Spanish.  We can offer
This role offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to a multi-stakeholder organisation driving positive global change. 

Located in central Oslo, the EITI International Secretariat offers hybrid work options, attractive benefits and an above-market pension and insurance package. Om arbeidsgiveren:

The Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) is the global standard to promote the open and accountable management of oil, gas and mineral resources.

Guided by the belief that a country’s natural resources belong to its citizens, the EITI has established a global standard to promote the open and accountable management of oil, gas and mineral resources. The EITI Standard requires the disclosure of information along the extractive industry value chain from the point of extraction, to how revenues make their way through the government, and how they benefit the public. By doing so, the EITI seeks to strengthen public and corporate governance, promote understanding of natural resource management, and provide the data to inform reforms for greater transparency and accountability in the extractives sector. In each of the 55 implementing countries, the EITI is supported by a coalition of government, companies, and civil society.

The EITI is committed to achieving diversity in terms of gender, nationality, culture and educational background. The EITI is an equal opportunities employer.

The Opportunity
Fossefall is building the infrastructure needed to power Europe's AI future. As our GPU and AI data centre projects move from design and procurement into construction, testing and operational readiness, we need a Commissioning Manager who can turn our commissioning strategy into a coordinated, evidence-based delivery plan.

Reporting to the VP Commissioning, you will lead owner-side project commissioning from design review and factory testing through installation verification, start-up, integrated systems testing and handover. You will connect engineering, construction, suppliers, Operations and IT delivery, identify gaps early and provide clear recommendations on readiness and acceptance. The role is based in Oslo with a hybrid working model and regular travel to project sites and supplier facilities.
What you'll do
• 
Develop and maintain the project Commissioning Plan, scope, schedule, resource plan and readiness gates, integrated with construction, utility availability and phased delivery.

• 
Review designs and supplier documentation for testability, maintainability and operational requirements.

• 
Coordinate the full L1-L5 commissioning process: factory testing, installation QA/QC and static tests, start-up and pre-functional checks, system or module SAT and integrated systems testing.

• 
Review and coordinate test method statements, scripts, load profiles, acceptance criteria, sequences of operation and cause-and-effect coverage with engineering SMEs, contractors, OEMs and the independent Commissioning Authority where appointed.

• 
Secure test prerequisites, including permanent or temporary power, load banks, thermal loads, cooling readiness, water quality, calibrated instruments, controls connectivity and safe working arrangements.

• 
Coordinate electrical, mechanical and liquid-cooling systems, BMS, EPMS and DCIM, fire and life safety, security and ICT/OT interfaces. Align facility readiness with rack, server, cluster and platform delivery leads.

• 
Use Omega365 as the system of record for commissioning scope, checklists, test evidence, digital sign-off, punch and NCR status, retests and readiness reporting.

• 
Manage commissioning risks, blockers, changes and deferred tests. Escalate failed acceptance criteria and readiness gaps with clear evidence and recommended actions.

• 
Prepare readiness recommendations, including RFC before L4, RFS following successful integrated systems testing and RFT after the agreed IT and service-validation scope.

• 
Coordinate Operations training, O&M deliverables, handover, the final commissioning report and the outstanding-item register.
About you
• 
Typically 5+ years of experience in commissioning or delivery of complex technical facilities, including responsibility for multidisciplinary commissioning.

• 
A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Automation, Energy Systems or a related technical discipline. Equivalent practical experience from commissioning complex technical facilities may compensate for formal education.

• 
Strong working knowledge of power and cooling infrastructure, controls integration, functional testing, failure scenarios and integrated systems testing.

• 
Experience leading contractors, OEMs and specialist test teams through clear plans, responsibilities, decisions and escalation, including teams without a direct reporting line.

• 
The judgement to challenge test methods, assess evidence, manage cross-discipline interfaces and make clear recommendations on system readiness.

• 
A structured, pragmatic and decisive working style. You communicate technical risks clearly and follow issues through to verified closure.

• 
Fluent professional English, both written and spoken, and willingness to travel and work on site during critical testing periods.

• 
Experience from owner-side commissioning in data centres or other mission-critical environments, modular facilities, GPU or AI infrastructure, liquid cooling or first-of-kind systems would be valuable. So would experience with Omega365 or comparable digital commissioning tools, Norwegian or another Scandinavian language and a relevant commissioning or project management certification, but none of these is required.
What success looks like
Within the first few months, project commissioning is governed by a clear and trusted plan, testing is prepared before site execution and readiness decisions are supported by complete, traceable evidence. Engineering, construction, suppliers, Operations and IT delivery understand their responsibilities and interfaces. Risks are surfaced early, defects and deferred tests are controlled and handover is completed without avoidable gaps between facility readiness and technology deployment.
Why Fossefall?
This is an opportunity to shape owner-side commissioning capability while Fossefall's AI infrastructure portfolio is being built. You will work across the physical and digital layers of high-performance AI facilities, influence how projects move from construction into reliable operation and collaborate with specialists across engineering, project delivery, operations and technology.

We are still small enough for individual judgement and ownership to matter. You will have room to improve how we work, contribute to critical delivery decisions and help build repeatable commissioning practices for future projects.
About Fossefall
Fossefall is a Nordic AI infrastructure company founded in 2025. We develop and operate AI factories powered by renewable energy, turning clean Nordic power into scalable, sovereign computing capacity for Europe, built in partnership with local communities, energy producers and technology leaders across the world. As a team, we are still small enough to know each other as people, and our culture is shaped by ownership, curiosity, warmth and collaboration.
Interested?
Make sure your CV is up to date for this role and tell us briefly why this opportunity is interesting to you and how your experience connects to what we are looking for. We review applications as they come in and keep the role open until we find the right colleague. Due to the nature of our business, background checks and/or security clearance may be required as part of the employment process.

About ZEEKR

ZEEKR is a premium electric mobility brand within Geely Holding Group, combining advanced technology with Scandinavian design. As we continue to develop our business in Norway through a dealer model, we are looking for a Business Operations & Claims Specialist to support our local sales organisation.

The Role

As Business Operations & Claims Specialist, you will be part of the local sales organisation in Norway, supporting the financial administration and operational processes that enable the business and dealer network to run smoothly.

You will coordinate dealer claims, bonus schemes and sales incentives, follow up on invoices and payments, and support procurement and local administrative activities. Working closely with dealers, Sales, Marketing, Finance, suppliers and HQ, you will help ensure accurate records, timely follow-up and effective ways of working.

Key Responsibilities

Dealer Claims, Bonuses & Sales Incentives from a Sales perspective 

•	Administer and follow up on dealer claims, bonus schemes and sales incentives in accordance with applicable guidelines.

•	Review claims against scheme terms, supporting documentation and sales data, and coordinate approvals with relevant stakeholders and HQ.

•	Follow up on missing documentation, discrepancies and exceptions with dealers and internal teams.

•	Track submitted, processed and outstanding claims, ensuring accurate records and timely resolution.

•	Act as a point of contact for dealers on claims, bonus schemes and sales incentives.

•	Prepare claims and incentive reports for the Sales team.

•	Support accurate sales reporting by checking relevant data and following up on discrepancies.

Procurement & Supplier Invoice Coordination

•	Coordinate local purchase requests and purchase orders, including creation and tracking, and provide information on outstanding commitments to the Finance Business Partner as needed

•	Support vendor onboarding, supplier master data and procurement administration in coordination with HQ.

•	Coordinate supplier agreements and contract documentation in line with HQ procurement policies and approval requirements.

Local Operations & Administrative Support

•	Maintain accurate customer master data.

•	Support the administration of customer, warranty and commercial claims in coordination with HQ.

•	Coordinate day-to-day administration for the local organisation, including office facilities, leases, utilities, telecommunications and other operational needs.

•	Coordinate local operational suppliers, contracts, service agreements and renewals.

•	Act as a local administrative point of contact for suppliers and internal stakeholders, helping resolve day-to-day issues.

Business Support & Process Improvements

•	Support the Finance Business Partner and coordinate with HQ Finance and other relevant teams on operational financial and administrative matters.

•	Support the Finance Business Partner and relevant stakeholders during audits and compliance reviews by providing operational documentation and records.

•	Identify and communicate opportunities to improve operational processes and documentation related to claims, incentives, invoicing and administration.

Qualifications

•	Bsc. degree in business administration, finance or a related field or relevant vocational training is an advantage. Relevant work experience may be considered instead of formal qualifications.

•	2-3+ years of work experience.

•	Experience in administration, sales support, invoicing, claims handling or a similar coordination role. 

•	Good organisational skills and attention to detail.

•	Comfortable working with numbers, records and spreadsheets, including basic Excel.

•	Ability to follow procedures, manage several tasks and meet deadlines.

•	Clear communication skills and a service-minded approach when working with colleagues, dealers and suppliers.

•	Willingness to learn new systems and processes and ask questions when needed.

•	Experience with dealer networks, automotive businesses, claims or incentive schemes is an advantage, but not required.

•	Norwegian and English language skills appropriate for communicating with local dealers and international colleagues.
